items.title: Fred Wesley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 21, 2024
items.q: Pee Wee Ellis had made it so that it would be an interesting song you know. And so I liked it... But so but that’s why I stayed with James Brown.

ctx.x: Was there a point during college or after that you had to make a decision about, financially, what kind of music should I be playing? Should I pursue being in the jazz world or did things just happen to you to steer you in another direction?

Things just happened to me to steer me in another direction. I took the job with James Brown with the intent of getting to a large city — I come from a small town in Alabama — Mobile, Alabama — and you know it’s not much chance of being heard and being known as a jazz musician in Mobile, Alabama. You know? So I wanted to get to New York and I wanted to get to L.A. or Chicago, somewhere where I could be heard — to play the jazz that I knew I could play you know. But so I took the job with James Brown but I had no…
And you’re still touring? Good for you, man. I think it keeps you young I believe.
